m:gamla: Free to walk and the streets are always open. Shops and cafés are usually open from 10am to 6pm. The Stortorget Christmas market is planned from 21 November to 23 December 2026 (dates to be confirmed: they're usually published in October).
m:slottet: According to the official website the Palace was open from 10am to 5pm on the day I checked; in low season some rooms close on certain days and can close at the last minute for state ceremonies (check kungligaslotten.se). An adult ticket costs about 270 kronor (the official table is confusing: to be confirmed). The changing of the guard is usually around 12:15pm, on Sundays and holidays around 1:15pm, with fewer days in winter.
m:nobel: Adult ticket 160 kronor in 2026 (official website); students and over-65s 120 kronor; free up to age 18. The hours I read in a guide are 10am–6pm every day and until 8pm on Tuesdays (to be confirmed on nobelprizemuseum.se). Closed on 1 January, 24 and 25 December.
m:stadshuset: The guided tour runs at fixed times every day, but may be cancelled for council events (check stadshuset.stockholm). I couldn't find the price on an up-to-date page: check it on the website. The tower is only open from May to mid-August and in 2027–2028 will be closed for restoration, so in autumn you can't go up. Tickets are sold online or at the ticket office, which opens at 8:30am.
m:vasa: Open from September to May from 10am to 5pm, Wednesdays until 8pm; closed on 24 and 25 December; 31 December 10am–3pm (official 2026 listing). Adult ticket 195 kronor from 1 October to 31 December and from 1 January to 30 April; free up to age 18. Take tram 7 to the Nordiska museet/Vasamuseet stop.
m:skansen: Open every day of the year. From 28 September 2026 to 10 January 2027 the hours are 10am–3pm on weekdays and 10am–4pm at weekends (official website), with exceptions: Christmas market from 27 November to 20 December (Friday and Saturday 10am–5pm, Sunday 10am–4pm), Christmas Eve 10am–2pm, New Year's Eve 10am–4pm and in the evening 8pm–midnight, Halloween on 24 and 28 to 31 October with evening opening 3–7pm. I didn't read the entry price in official form: one guide gives 305 kronor in high season; in winter it costs less (check skansen.se). Entrances and shops take electronic payments only.
m:abba: Hours generally between 10am and 6pm, longer in summer (from guides and articles, to be confirmed on abbathemuseum.com). Tickets have dynamic prices, from about 250 to 330 kronor depending on day and time: best to book a time slot online.
m:fotog: Open every day from 10am to 11pm; on 24 December it closes at 8pm (official FAQ page). Adult ticket 195 kronor, students and under-25s 135 kronor; on Wednesdays from 6pm two tickets for the price of one. Exhibitions change every few months: see the programme on fotografiska.com.
m:monte: It's free and open 24 hours a day, all year. From Mariatorget metro (red line) it's about 5 minutes on foot, from Slussen about 10 minutes up a steep climb. In autumn and winter sunset is early (before 4pm in December) and the ground can be slippery with ice.
m:historiska: From September to May open Tuesday to Sunday from 11am to 5pm, Wednesdays until 8pm; closed on Mondays (official 2026 information). Adult ticket 180 kronor (price without a year in the listing; to be confirmed); free up to age 18.
m:saluhall: Open Monday to Friday 9:30am–7pm (some guides say until 8pm on Fridays), Saturday 9:30am–5pm, closed on Sundays. The market is expensive: stall dishes range from 95 to 225 kronor, restaurants with tables from 245 to 395 kronor. Pay by card.
vd:gyldene: A 1722 inn in Gamla Stan, run as a meeting place by the Swedish Academy: classic Swedish cooking in dark wooden rooms with candles. This is where to try Nordic food in a historic setting.
vp:gyldene: Meatballs with mash and lingonberries cost about 270 kronor (about €24); main courses start at around 300 kronor (menu not read on the website). Hours from a 2025 guide, to be confirmed.
vd:vete: The Swedes' favourite café-pâtisserie, open since 1928: a display of cakes, biscuits and cinnamon buns (kanelbulle) in a bright old salon. Perfect for breakfast or a fika break.
vp:vete: A coffee with a cinnamon bun costs about €8–10 (menu not seen on the website). I wrote the hours from general knowledge and didn't read them on an up-to-date page: to be confirmed.
vd:saluhall: The historic food hall of the smart district: among the stalls are small restaurants with shrimp sandwiches, fish soup, dishes of the day and sweets. Eat standing or at little tables, surrounded by the smell of fresh fish.
vp:saluhall: Stall dishes range from 95 to 225 kronor (about €8.50–20), restaurants with tables from 245 to 395 kronor (about €22–35). Lisa Elmqvist's shrimp sandwich is between 145 and 225 kronor. Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:hotorget: The food hall beneath the concert hall, near Central Station: Greek, Middle Eastern, South American and Asian stalls, with fish, cheeses, gyros and pasta at lower prices than Östermalm. Perfect for a quick lunch.
vp:hotorget: A meal is between 95 and 175 kronor (about €8.50–15.50): gyros 95–125, pasta 125–175, fish 125–195 (unofficial guide). Card or Swish only. Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:saturnus: A neighbourhood café known for its huge cinnamon buns the size of a plate and hearty breakfasts, in bright rooms with wooden tables. Popular with families and residents.
vp:saturnus: A coffee with a cinnamon bun costs about €8–10 (menu not seen). The opening time (from 7:30am) is confirmed by a guide; evening closing and weekends to be checked.
vd:mfp: A restaurant that does only meatballs: beef, pork, elk, chicken or vegetarian, with creamy mashed potato, gravy and lingonberries. The right place to try Swedish meatballs without ending up in a tourist trap.
vp:mfp: A dish costs about 230 kronor (about €20.50); the eight-meatball tasting for two or three people about 330 kronor each (guides). In the evening it's best to book a week ahead; at lunch there's usually room.
vd:blaporten: A café-restaurant in a yellow house with a courtyard, a short walk from Skansen and ABBA The Museum: simple Swedish dishes like meatballs, salmon and soups, homemade cakes.
vp:blaporten: Meatballs cost about 208 kronor (about €18.50) (unofficial guide). Hours from a 2025 guide, to be confirmed.
vd:rosendal: The café in the biodynamic garden and glasshouses on the east side of Djurgården: bread from the wood-fired oven, seasonal vegetable soups, cakes with fruit from the garden. In October and November you eat in the heated glasshouses.
vp:rosendal: Lunch (11am to 2:30pm) costs about 150–200 kronor (about €13.50–18) (estimate from guides, menu not read). No bookings. Hours from the official website 'Mon–Sun 11am–4pm'; in winter they may be shorter: check rosendalstradgard.se.
vd:kalf: A small place on Mariatorget square serving one typical dish, the «Stockholm»: three meatballs with bread and pickled vegetables, and little else. A quick Swedish meal to take away or eat at the counter.
vp:kalf: The «Stockholm» dish with bread and three meatballs costs about 110 kronor (about €9.80) (2025 guide, to be confirmed). Hours from a guide, to be checked.
vd:soderhallarna: Södermalm's food hall, next to Medborgarplatsen square: pizza by the slice, sandwiches, soups, meatballs and sweets at different stalls, for reasonably priced lunches in a lively district.
vp:soderhallarna: A slice of pizza costs between 45 and 85 kronor (about €4–7.50), a full meal 95–175 kronor (about €8.50–15.50) (unofficial guide). Card or Swish only. Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
cd:modernamuseet: Picasso, Dalí and Warhol on the island of Skeppsholmen.
cd:nordiska: Swedish everyday life over five centuries, in a neo-Renaissance palace.
cd:gronalund: The amusement park on the island of Djurgården.
cx:gronalund: Only open in some months: check the calendar.
cd:arcipelago: Two hours by boat among the islets around the city.
cd:millesgarden: The house and terraced garden of the sculptor Carl Milles.
cx:millesgarden: It's on the island of Lidingö, about 6 km from the centre.
cd:kaknas: The 155-metre TV tower, with a 360-degree view.
cd:skyview: A cabin rides up the stadium's huge sphere: views from 130 metres.
